description: CRYPTO_SPEC §5.2: commitment of the epoch DEK. dek_commitment_hex = lower_hex(SHA-256(LP("<suite>/dek-commit", project_id, environment_id, epoch, dek_hex))). The DEK and coordinates are identical to the basic vector in dek-wrap.json
binary_encoding: dek_hex is placed on the LP as the lowercase hex string of the 32-byte DEK (same convention as binary_encoding in chain-entries.json)

rewrap_invariance.note: The commitment preimage does not depend on the wrap or the recipient (§5.2): the commitment is invariant across backfill of past epochs after add_member, deletion → re-registration of a repair path, variation of the wrap ciphertext for the same DEK due to HPKE randomness, and post-hoc expansion of the recipient set. The implementation test pins that re-wrapping the same DEK afresh (HPKE Seal is randomized) yields a DEK that verifies against this commitment once unwrapped
rewrap_invariance.wrap_reference: dek-wrap.json vectors[0] (actual wrap data of the same DEK)

vectors.name: basic
vectors.note: Same DEK and coordinates as basic in dek-wrap.json (epoch 3 — derived from rotate)

vectors.name: epoch-1-create
vectors.note: Commitment for epoch 1 (derived from create_environment — §6.2). Because the coordinates enter the preimage, the value differs from basic

negative.name: dek-mismatch
negative.note: A different DEK fails commitment verification (blocks fake-DEK injection — §5.2 / §14.2-1)

negative.name: transplant-project
negative.note: Does not match a commitment under different project coordinates (the coordinates enter the preimage)

negative.name: transplant-environment
negative.note: Does not match a commitment under different environment coordinates

negative.name: transplant-epoch
negative.note: Does not match a commitment under different epoch coordinates

negative.name: wrong-domain
negative.note: A different suite means a different domain string, so transplanting a commitment across suites fails verification

negative.name: uppercase-hex
negative.note: An uppercase-hex dek_hex becomes a different byte string and fails verification (the canonical form of the preimage is lowercase hex — implementations must normalize the input to lowercase hex before computing)
